summary: Samoa Immigration says visitors to Samoa can apply for a 90-day Visitor Permit on arrival using the arrival card, and must have a passport valid for at least 6 months beyond the intended stay, confirmed onward tickets, visas for the next country of destination, sufficient funds to support themselves and a confirmed residential contact address. Its border page says foreign nationals who do not hold a valid Temporary Resident Permit or Samoan citizenship will be issued with a free 90-day Visitors Permit upon arrival.

vaccinations.text: The UK government says you must have a certificate to prove you have had a yellow fever vaccination if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk. WHO's country list gives Samoa's requirement as proof of vaccination for travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from countries with risk of yellow fever transmission, and for travellers who have transited for more than 12 hours through an airport of such a country.

safety.text: The UK government says the level of serious crime is low and incidents of petty theft are uncommon and opportunistic. It says Samoa's tides can produce powerful currents in ocean lagoons and many waves break directly onto reefs, advises taking local advice before swimming or surfing, and says stray dogs are common in Apia and in many villages.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says the sale of alcohol is prohibited on Sundays. The UK's says drinking alcohol in public is illegal except at bars or restaurants, and that the legal drinking age is 21.

The UK government's travel advice says local communities expect you to dress modestly when visiting towns and villages, and that swimwear is acceptable on the beach or by streams and waterfalls but anywhere else is likely to receive negative attention. Canada's advises not taking photos of individuals without explicit permission, and requesting permission before entering a lagoon, as certain villages may hold customary rights over them.

Canada's travel advice says traffic drives on the left. The UK government tells British drivers they must buy a temporary driving permit, which requires a UK driving licence; car rental companies will help with this, and the permit can be used for up to 90 days a year. It says the speed limit is 40 km/h in towns and villages and 56 km/h outside, and that any accident must be reported to the police within 24 hours.
Canada's travel advice says ATMs are mostly located in and around Apia, with one on Savai'i, and that they remain unavailable throughout the rest of the islands.
The UK government's travel advice says the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to the end of April, and that higher rainfall inland can cause flooding.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Samoa?
faq.answer: Samoa Immigration says foreign nationals who do not hold a valid Temporary Resident Permit or Samoan citizenship will be issued with a free 90-day Visitors Permit upon arrival, applied for using the arrival card. Travellers must have a passport valid for at least 6 months beyond the intended stay, confirmed onward tickets, visas for the next country of destination, sufficient funds to support themselves and a confirmed residential contact address.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Samoa?
faq.answer: Samoa Immigration says visitors can apply for a 90-day Visitor Permit on arrival. Visitors in Samoa who wish to stay longer as a visitor use the temporary residence form (MPMC100), with a photocopy of an onward ticket out of Samoa, evidence of sufficient funds to support the extended stay and details of their accommodation arrangements.

faq.question: Do I need a return ticket to enter Samoa?
faq.answer: Yes. Samoa Immigration says the grant of a Visitors permit is subject to its entry requirements, including that the passenger must have a return or onward ticket and state their accommodation arrangements, be it holiday accommodation such as a hotel or resort, or with family or friends (specifically the village and family name).

faq.question: What vaccinations do I need for Samoa?
faq.answer: The UK government says you must have a certificate to prove you have had a yellow fever vaccination if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk. Samoa's Ministry of Health says it has no active travel advisories or health-related travel restrictions in place at this time. The UK government lists Zika virus and dengue among the health risks and says to take precautions against being bitten by mosquitoes.

countryFacts.driving.text: All international drivers are required to get an endorsement on their full drivers’ licence before they are allowed to drive in Samoa. Temporary drivers’ permits are available from most rental vehicle companies, or you could visit the Samoa Tourism Information Center, Samoa Post, or the Samoa Land Transport Authority in Apia.

A driving permit costs WST$21 for one month, but car rental companies may charge a fee on top of this. Once issued, an endorsed international drivers’ licence can only be used for a maximum period of 90 days in any one year; a longer period requires a Samoan drivers’ licence.
